tasks.short: Pull labour market data (CBS, UWV, CAO wage tables, agency rate cards) into one sheet for HR.

today.trigger: Monthly HR management meeting, a budget round, or a question from the HR Director about pay or labour shortage in a region.
steps: Visit CBS StatLine, UWV, and the CAO and sector sites for new figures
Download the agency rate cards and invoices from the three staffing portals
Copy the figures into an Excel workbook by site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo)
Write source and date next to each figure
Send the workbook to the HRBP or HR Director who asked
drudgery: Re-finding the same tables every month
Copying numbers by hand and retyping source notes
today.time_sinks: Finding the latest version of each source and putting different regional and job definitions on one basis.

lenses.faster: A scheduled job fetches the fixed public tables and agency files, and a model pulls the figures out of PDFs with page references; the analyst only checks the flagged changes, so about 75 hours a year drops to about 30.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly timer or a new agency invoice starts the run; fetching, extracting and citing run unattended, and the analyst approves the sheet before it goes to SharePoint.
lenses.ambitious: A new service for the three HRBPs: a monthly one-page labour market brief per site with pay and agency rate figures for order pickers, drivers and forklift operators. Demand would grow if it got cheaper, because recruiters would use it in every offer talk.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss re-downloading and retyping tables; the analyst wants more time to work out which figures actually explain hiring problems in Venlo.
lenses.options: Little value in several drafts here; the job is gathering, and one correct, sourced set is what counts.
lenses.altitude: The analyst spends an hour a month choosing and checking sources instead of a day collecting them, and decides which outside sources count as official for HR.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: keeping the CAO wage table and market pay reference up to date (needs CAO scale knowledge)
FP&A Analyst: agency rate inputs for the flex budget (needs the finance cost model)

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a source is reliable and comparable (job definitions, region, date), and spotting when a sudden change is a definition change and not a real trend.
tasks.pattern_why: The sources and fields are known in advance; one model call per document turns PDFs and web tables into a checkable table with citations.

in_practice.trigger: First working day of the month, or a new rate card or invoice in a staffing agency portal.
steps: Script downloads the fixed CBS and UWV tables and the agency files
Model extracts figures from PDFs into a fixed table with page and URL
Script compares with last month and flags changes above a set threshold
Analyst checks flagged rows and approves
Approved sheet is saved to SharePoint and the Power BI labour market page refreshes
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves the monthly sheet before it is published to HR.
data_needed: List of approved sources with URLs
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list with source URL, fetch date, extracted value and approver.

evidence.claim: Model extraction of figures from PDFs and web tables into a structured table is routine today.
Trend summaries should keep the source's own caveats; Workday's report says its data does not establish how much of the decline AI caused.

risks: Silent extraction errors from scanned agency PDFs
Website layout changes break the fetch without warning
Purchased sources may forbid automated download
research_questions: Which of the current sources offer an API or stable download, and which only PDFs?
How often did the HRBPs actually use last year's labour market figures in a decision?
Do agency contracts allow rate data to be processed by an outside model?

tasks.short: Tell HR and managers what changed in dashboards, reports and metric definitions.

today.trigger: A Power BI release, a new measure, a changed definition (for example verzuim percentage), or repeated questions from managers.
steps: Note what changed in the Power BI model or report
Write an email or Teams post explaining the change
Update the explanation page in SharePoint
Answer follow-up questions from HRBPs and site managers one by one
drudgery: Writing the same explanation in three places
Answering the same 'what does this number mean' questions
today.time_sinks: Follow-up questions after each release, because managers did not read or understand the note.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the release note and the glossary update from the change log and measure descriptions; the analyst edits for five minutes instead of writing for an hour, and a Teams answer bot handles repeat questions.
lenses.autonomous: Publishing a new Power BI version starts the draft; the analyst approves the note, then it posts to the HR Teams channel and SharePoint.
lenses.ambitious: Serve site and shift managers in Tilburg and Venlo for the first time with a Teams bot that explains each metric in Dutch, marked as AI under EU AI Act Art. 50; demand grows as managers learn they can ask.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping release notes; the analyst wants more time sitting with managers to learn which numbers they actually use.
lenses.options: Two versions of a note (short for managers, detailed for HRBPs) change who reads it, but not the decision; low value beyond that.
lenses.altitude: The analyst writes each definition once and decides which ones are official; the week has fewer interruptions and more time on the metric layer.
reach: HR Business Partner: explaining dashboards to line managers (needs coaching and site context)
L&D Specialist: short Studytube module on reading the HR dashboard (needs course-building skills)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change will upset a manager or the works council, and how to say it so it is understood on the warehouse floor.
tasks.pattern_why: The input (change log, measure descriptions) and output (note, glossary entry) are fixed; one model call drafts it inside a set release routine.

in_practice.trigger: New version of the HR Power BI semantic model or report published.
steps: Script exports the changed measures and descriptions
Model drafts a release note in Dutch and English and updates the glossary entry
Analyst edits and approves
Note posts to Teams and SharePoint; glossary feeds the manager Q&A bot
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves every note before it is posted.
systems: Copilot in Power BI or Claude
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint release log with version, note and approver.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI summarises reports and works on a semantic model; non-English chat is not officially supported.
Chatbots used with workers must say they are AI.

risks: Dutch output quality from Copilot not officially supported
A wrong definition spreads faster when posted automatically
research_questions: How many follow-up questions does a typical release produce today?
Do site managers read Teams posts, or does the message need to go via the shift lead?
Is Noordhaven on Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity for Copilot?

tasks.short: Write specs for new HR dashboards and reports: fields, definitions, filters, access.

today.trigger: A request from the HR Director, an HRBP, Finance or the works council for a new report or dashboard.
steps: Interview the requester about what they want to see
Check which AFAS and Recruitee fields exist
Write a spec in Word with measures, filters, row-level security and refresh
Review with the requester and adjust
Store the spec in SharePoint
drudgery: Looking up field names and table structures again
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth with requesters whose wish is vague, and checking which source fields really hold the data.

lenses.faster: From the meeting transcript and the AFAS data dictionary the model drafts the spec, suggests DAX and lists missing fields; the analyst keeps the interview and the decisions, cutting 73 hours to about 45.
lenses.autonomous: Not autonomous: the analyst runs the intake and uses the draft as a starting point.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the Controller and FP&A: shared specs for headcount and personnel cost so HR and Finance report one number; demand would grow as both sides stop reconciling.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses formatting specs and hunting field names; the analyst wants more time on the intake conversation that clarifies what decision the report supports.
lenses.options: Two or three mock-up layouts shown to the requester change what gets built and often reveal the real question; worth doing.
lenses.altitude: The analyst becomes the gate for what enters the metric layer and decides definitions and access rules; the work gets more expert.
reach: FP&A Analyst: specs for personnel cost reports (needs the general ledger structure)
Recruiter: Recruitee funnel report specs (needs pipeline stage knowledge)

tasks.human_edge: Finding the decision behind a request, saying no to reports that would need works council consent or would expose individuals, and setting access.
tasks.pattern_why: The analyst leads the intake and every design choice; AI drafts text, DAX and checks fields.

in_practice.trigger: New report request logged in the HR request list.
steps: Analyst holds the intake in Teams with transcription on
Copilot drafts the spec from the transcript and the data dictionary
Analyst fixes definitions, access and privacy notes
Requester signs off in SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst and requester sign off on the spec; privacy check by analyst before build.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint spec library with version history.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI writes DAX and works on a prepared semantic model; without one it can misinterpret the data.
Dashboards able to observe behaviour or performance need works council consent under WOR 27(1)(l).

risks: Draft invents AFAS fields that do not exist
Spec looks complete and skips the privacy and consent check
research_questions: Does an up-to-date AFAS data dictionary exist, or must it be built first?
How many requests per year turn out to need works council consent?
How much of spec time is intake versus writing?

tasks.short: Turn HR trend data into recommendations for the HR Director, like retention or flex use per site.

today.trigger: Quarterly HR review, budget planning, or a spike such as falling 90-day retention in Venlo.
steps: Pull trends from Power BI and AFAS extracts
Add outside context (labour market, CAO changes)
Look for causes by site, shift and agency
Write a short memo with two or three recommendations
Present to the HR Director or MT
drudgery: Building the same charts each quarter
today.time_sinks: Cutting the data many ways to find what explains a change, then writing it up clearly.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the trend summary and charts from the quarterly data and lists possible explanations with the evidence; the analyst tests them and writes the recommendation, saving about a third.
lenses.autonomous: Low autonomy: a quarterly run prepares the pack, the analyst does the reasoning and owns the memo.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: a monthly instead of quarterly retention and flex-mix review per site with the site managers, so action on Venlo order pickers comes in weeks, not a quarter; demand would grow if cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding charts; the analyst wants more time testing explanations with site managers.
lenses.options: Strong: scenarios such as more permanent contracts versus more agency hours, with cost and retention effects side by side, change the choice the HR Director makes.
lenses.altitude: The analyst shifts from making packs to advising on hiring mix and onboarding, and gets a seat in site planning; the job becomes more expert.
reach: FP&A Analyst: flex versus permanent cost scenarios (needs cost modelling)
HR Business Partner: preparing site action plans (needs site relationships)

tasks.human_edge: Telling causes from coincidences, knowing site history and politics, and owning a recommendation people can act on.
tasks.pattern_why: The reasoning and recommendation stay with the analyst; AI speeds up slicing, charting and first drafts.

in_practice.trigger: Quarter close, or a metric crossing a set threshold.
steps: Power BI refresh produces the trend pack
Copilot drafts a summary and possible explanations with numbers
Analyst tests explanations and builds scenarios
Analyst writes and presents the recommendation
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst owns every recommendation; nothing goes to MT unchecked.
data_needed: 90-day retention, absence rate, time to hire by site
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint memo archive with data snapshot date.

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent warns faster access to information does not by itself lead to better decisions.
Trend data does not establish cause; keep such caveats.

risks: Small groups per shift make trends noisy and can identify people
research_questions: Which past recommendations were acted on, and what happened?
Are group sizes per site and shift large enough for monthly review?
Would site managers attend a monthly review?

tasks.short: Test that HR reports and figures match the source and the agreed definitions.

today.trigger: Before a new report goes live, after an AFAS change, or when a manager says a number looks wrong.
steps: Pick sample employees and periods
Compare Power BI totals with AFAS and payroll figures
Check filters, definitions and row-level security
Log differences and fix the model or ask HR admin to correct AFAS
Confirm with the requester
drudgery: Re-running the same checks after every change
today.time_sinks: Tracing why headcount or verzuim differs between AFAS and Power BI.

lenses.faster: Reconciliation tests and data quality checks (missing end dates, open sick reports, contract gaps) run after each nightly refresh; the analyst only looks at failures, cutting about 68 hours to under 30.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract triggers the test suite; passing runs need nobody, failures go to the analyst and data errors to HR admin.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the manager Q&A bot: a test set of verified questions and answers that every bot answer is checked against, so managers can trust self-service figures; demand rises as more managers use it.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses Excel reconciliations; the analyst wants more time fixing root causes in AFAS processes.
lenses.options: Little value; tests either pass or fail.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the quality rules for HR data and can block a release; HR admin gets a clear daily correction list.
reach: HR Administrator: daily AFAS data quality checks (needs AFAS entry rules)
Payroll Specialist: headcount and FTE reconciliation before month close (needs payroll run knowledge)

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what the correct definition is when AFAS, payroll and Finance disagree, and judging whether a difference matters.
tasks.pattern_why: Checks and reconciliations can be written as rules and SQL; no model is needed to run them.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract and Power BI refresh complete.
steps: Test suite reconciles totals with AFAS and payroll
Rules flag missing end dates, open sick reports and other gaps
Failures create a list for HR admin and alert the analyst
Verified Q&A set is re-run against the manager bot
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst decides on release blocks and definition disputes; HR admin corrects source data.
in_practice.logs_to: Test result table with date, test, outcome and owner.

evidence.claim: Rule-based checks for AFAS data quality (missing end dates, open sick reports) suit deterministic software at autonomy 4.
Text-to-SQL still hallucinates tables and columns, so generated answers need tests against verified results.

risks: Tests give false comfort if definitions are wrong
Absence checks must never touch sickness causes (GDPR Art. 9)
research_questions: How many report errors did managers find last year, and what caused them?
Does the AFAS extract allow a reliable reconciliation with payroll per month?
Who owns the definition register today?

tasks.short: Track what competing employers and agencies offer warehouse and transport staff in our regions.

today.trigger: Hard-to-fill roles, a recruiter reporting lost candidates, or annual pay review.
steps: Scan job sites for competitor vacancies in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
Note pay, shifts, bonuses and contract offers
Compare with Noordhaven's CAO scale and agency rates
Write a summary for recruiters and the Comp and Ben Specialist
drudgery: Reading many vacancy texts by hand
today.time_sinks: Collecting enough comparable vacancies to say anything about pay and offers.

lenses.faster: A model extracts pay, shift premium, contract type and perks from collected vacancy texts into a table; the analyst reviews the summary, cutting about 61 hours to about 30.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly run collects and extracts; the analyst approves the summary before it goes to recruiters.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: recruiters check offers against current regional competitor pay at each offer for order pickers and drivers, instead of once a year; demand would grow with lower cost.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying vacancy texts; the analyst wants more time linking competitor offers to Noordhaven's offer acceptance rate.
lenses.options: Showing two or three offer packages against the market changes what the Comp and Ben Specialist proposes; useful.
lenses.altitude: The analyst gives recruiters and comp and ben a live market view and gets a say in offer ranges; somewhat more expert.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: market pay benchmarking (needs job grading knowledge)
Recruiter: competitor offer insight for candidate talks (needs sourcing context)

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a vacancy is truly comparable and what it means for Noordhaven's offer, given CAO limits.
tasks.pattern_why: Fixed workflow: collect vacancy texts, one model call per text extracts a fixed set of fields, then rules aggregate.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly schedule, or offer acceptance rate dropping for a role.
steps: Collect vacancy texts for target roles and regions
Model extracts pay, shifts, contract and perks per vacancy
Script aggregates by role and region and compares with CAO scale
Analyst reviews and sends summary
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves the summary before it is shared.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint table with vacancy URL, extracted fields and run date.

evidence.claim: Model extraction of fixed fields from job ad text is routine.

risks: Job site terms may forbid scraping
Posted pay often missing or a range, giving biased comparisons
research_questions: What share of regional competitor vacancies state pay?
Do recruiters lose candidates on pay, shifts or something else?
Can job data be licensed instead of scraped?

tasks.short: Produce required HR reports: verzuim, social annual report for the OR, CBS surveys, headcount.

today.trigger: Monthly close, quarterly OR meeting, annual social report, or a CBS or insurer request.
steps: Run AFAS extracts and refresh Power BI
Copy figures into the report template
Check totals against last period
Write commentary
Send to HR Director, OR or the requesting body
drudgery: Copying the same figures into templates
today.time_sinks: Last-minute checks when figures differ from the previous version.

lenses.faster: Reports fill from the model automatically and a model drafts the commentary from the period's changes; the analyst checks and signs, cutting about 58 hours to about 22.
lenses.autonomous: The month or quarter close triggers the run; standard internal reports go out after checks pass, required filings and OR reports wait for the analyst's sign-off.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: flex workers and night shifts get their own lines in the verzuim and turnover reports for the OR, giving the works council a view it lacks; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses filling templates; the analyst wants more time explaining figures to the OR.
lenses.options: Little value; required reports need one correct version.
lenses.altitude: The analyst moves from producing reports to owning their definitions and sign-off, and becomes the OR's data contact.
reach: HR Administrator: CBS and insurer data requests (needs filing rules)
Controller: personnel figures for the annual report (needs financial reporting rules)

tasks.human_edge: Signing off figures that go to the OR or authorities, and explaining sensitive results to the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: Templates, sources and calculations are fixed; a model only drafts the narrative text.

steps: Extract and Power BI refresh
Tests reconcile totals
Templates fill automatically
Model drafts commentary on changes
Analyst reviews and signs before sending
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst signs each required filing and OR report.
data_needed: Headcount, contracts, verzuim rates and durations
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint report archive with version, data date and signer.

evidence.claim: Absence data is health data under GDPR Art. 9; verzuim analytics should hold rates and durations, never causes.
The Dutch AP fined a firm partly for recording the cause of sick leave.

risks: Generated commentary states causes the data cannot show
Small groups (flex, night shifts) can identify individuals
research_questions: Which reports are legally required versus custom?
Will the OR accept AI-drafted commentary if signed by the analyst?
What minimum group size does the OR and privacy officer require?

tasks.short: Keep the library of report templates, DAX measures, SQL snippets and spec templates up to date.

today.trigger: A new report built, a template outdated, or a colleague cannot find something.
steps: Save new templates and measures in SharePoint
Write descriptions and tags
Remove or mark outdated versions
Point colleagues to the right item
today.time_sinks: Library drifts out of date, so people rebuild what already exists.

lenses.faster: When an item is added, a model writes its description and tags and flags likely duplicates; the analyst approves, cutting about 53 hours to about 25.
lenses.autonomous: Saving an item triggers description, tagging and duplicate check; the analyst approves before it is marked official.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to FP&A and the Controller: a shared library of measures for headcount and personnel cost so both teams reuse the same logic; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses writing descriptions; the analyst wants more time improving the core measures.
lenses.altitude: The analyst curates what is official and retires the rest; less admin, same expertise.
reach: FP&A Analyst: shared measure library (needs finance definitions)
L&D Specialist: Studytube report templates (needs course data model)

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which version is official and which measures to retire.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call per new item writes a description and tags inside a fixed save routine.

in_practice.trigger: New or changed item in the SharePoint library.
steps: Model writes description and tags
Script checks for near-duplicates
Analyst approves and marks official
Glossary and search index update
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves before an item is marked official.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and approval column.

evidence.claim: Model-written descriptions and tags for documents and code snippets are routine.

risks: Duplicates missed when logic differs slightly
research_questions: How often are reports rebuilt because an existing one was not found?
Who besides the analyst uses the library?
Would Finance share one measure library?

role.altitude: From making reports to owning HR's metric layer: definitions, verified answers, tests and access rules that managers, Finance and AI agents query, with the right to block a release or a report that would need OR consent.
reach: HR Administrator: daily AFAS data quality checks
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: market pay benchmarking
FP&A Analyst: personnel cost and flex scenarios
Recruiter: Recruitee funnel reporting
Payroll Specialist: headcount reconciliation before month close
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about 540 of 1,600 hours a year, and roughly 45% of that time could go. The limits are AFAS data quality, works council consent for anything that can observe staff, GDPR Art. 9 on absence data, Copilot needing Fabric capacity and having weak Dutch support, and the 2027 high-risk rules for AI that evaluates workers.
skills_to_grow: Semantic model and metric definition design
role.ambitious_version: A self-service HR fact base in Teams for every site and shift manager, with tested answers for retention, verzuim rates and flex mix. Monthly site reviews would include flex workers, and the analyst would build and justify the workforce mix scenarios the MT decides on.
